question.subject: Introductory Physics
question.text: A sound wave of frequency 250 Hz has a wavelength of 1.36 m in air. What is the speed of sound in the air?
learning_objectives: W1 Use the wave equation v = f λ

question.subject: Introductory Physics
question.text: The velocity–time graph for a skateboarder moving in a straight line is shown below. Use the graph to determine the acceleration of the skateboarder.
learning_objectives: K1 Use the equations of uniformly accelerated motion
K2 Interpret motion data in tables and graphs
question.diagram_description: Velocity–time graph: velocity v / m s⁻¹ on the vertical axis (0 to 10), time t / s on the horizontal axis (0 to 6). A straight line runs from (0 s, 0 m/s) to (5.0 s, 9.0 m/s).

question.subject: Introductory Physics
question.text: When a student hangs a load on a spring of stiffness 40 N/m, it stretches by 0.19 m without passing its limit of proportionality. What force does the load exert on the spring?
learning_objectives: F2 Apply Hooke's law F = kx

constraints.text: the spring obeys Hooke's law (limit of proportionality not exceeded)

question.subject: Introductory Physics
question.text: The motor of a kitchen food mixer passes 2700 C of charge during 900 s of use. Calculate the average current in the motor.
learning_objectives: C2 Relate charge, current, potential difference and power

question.subject: Introductory Physics
question.text: A car of mass 1200 kg travels at 15 m/s. A lorry of mass 8000 kg travels at 2.5 m/s. Calculate the momentum of each vehicle and state which would need the larger average force to stop it in the same time.
learning_objectives: F1 Apply Newton's second law F = ma

marking.final_answer: car 18 000 kg m/s; lorry 20 000 kg m/s; the lorry needs the larger force
marking.worked_solution: p(car) = 1200 × 15 = 18 000 kg m/s; p(lorry) = 8000 × 2.5 = 20 000 kg m/s. Same stopping time ⇒ F = Δp/Δt is larger for the lorry.

points.description: Lorry: larger change of momentum in same time needs larger force

question.subject: Introductory Physics
question.text: A kettle connected to a 230 V supply draws a current of 8.0 A. The kettle and a toaster drawing 6.0 A are plugged into an adaptor protected by a 13 A fuse.
learning_objectives: C2 Relate charge, current, potential difference and power

constraints.text: the fuse melts if the total current exceeds 13 A

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the power of the kettle.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the energy transferred by the kettle in 150 s.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Determine whether the fuse melts when both appliances are switched on together.

marking.final_answer: (a) 1840 W (b) 2.8 × 10^5 J (c) yes: total current 14 A exceeds 13 A

question.subject: Introductory Physics
question.text: Travelling along a straight road at 20 m/s, a driver applies the brakes. The car decelerates uniformly and stops after covering 62 m.
learning_objectives: K1 Use the equations of uniformly accelerated motion
F3 Explain motion using Newton's first law

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the size of the car's deceleration.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find how long the car takes to stop.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain how an icy road surface would affect the stopping distance.

marking.final_answer: (a) 3.2 m/s² (b) 6.2 s (c) less friction on ice, so smaller deceleration and longer distance
marking.worked_solution: (a) a = u²/(2s) = 400/124 = 3.2 m/s² (b) t = u/a = 20/3.23 = 6.2 s (c) Ice reduces friction, so the maximum deceleration is smaller and the car travels further.

points.description: Smaller deceleration so longer stopping distance

question.subject: Introductory Physics
question.text: A motor lifts a 20 kg load through a vertical height of 5.0 m in 10 s. The graph shows the total energy supplied to the motor against time during the lift. Take g = 9.8 m/s².
learning_objectives: E1 Calculate gravitational potential and kinetic energy
K2 Interpret motion data in tables and graphs

given.description: energy supplied in 10 s (read from graph)

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the useful energy transferred to the load.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Use the graph to determine the input power to the motor.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Calculate the efficiency of the motor.

question.diagram_description: Graph of energy supplied E / J (vertical axis, 0 to 2500) against time t / s (horizontal axis, 0 to 12): a straight line through the origin reaching 2000 J at 10 s.
